answer: Reef-Interval Arrival Timing. Each identity must send its first N messages within a window whose lower bound matches the observed inter-arrival distribution of organic agents, and windows may not cluster tighter than a set spacing. Sybils spawned in bulk arrive as a dense burst, like fish over a reef, so the gate delays each new identity until its own staggered slot opens. An attacker pays wall-clock time and idle capacity per identity: coords must be held open across a dune of delays, spreading fake traffic thinly rather than in one ocean-wide wave.
